# Delta Refresh — stop re-fetching what has not changed

> ⚠️ **Status: In Review — awaiting Human Operator approval** (Constitution Art. II).
> 
> Tier 2, `updated` timestamps. Listed last in the report and deliberately specced last here — it is an optimisation, and optimisations should follow the things that change what the app can do.
## Intention
Every refresh re-fetches everything. The source publishes an `updated` timestamp on the records we read, so a refresh could skip what has not changed since it was last checked.
📊 **The scale that makes it worth stating:** 1,378 identified videos and 1,341 identified actors on the drive. A full refresh is ~2,700 requests, and rate limiting is already listed as an untested risk in the report — "our client declares a rate and has never been tested against a real limit".
## ⭐ D1 — The value is rate limit headroom, not speed
A faster refresh is pleasant. 🔴 The real gain is that several features now want library-wide sweeps — *What Else Are They In* (~50), Get More Photos (~315), enrich-the-unenriched, upstream-deletion checks — and they compete for the same budget. A delta turns a recurring 2,700-request operation into a small one, which is what makes the others affordable.
## ⚠️ D2 — We must record when WE last checked, and we mostly already do
`enrichmentCheckedAt` exists on profiles. ❓ **Open:** is there an equivalent on the video side, and is it reliably maintained? If not, this spec is really two — record the timestamp, then use it — and the first half must ship a release earlier so there is data to compare against.
🚨 A delta computed against a timestamp that is missing or wrong silently skips records that DID change, which is the worst possible failure for a refresh: it reports success and does nothing. That is this project's signature defect, and here it would be self-inflicted.
## 🔴 D3 — A full refresh must remain available and obvious
Whenever a delta is wrong, the recovery is a full pass. ⚠️ If the only refresh becomes the delta, a bug in the comparison is unrecoverable through the UI.
## D4 — Our schema changes invalidate the delta
🚨 The subtlety that will bite. "Unchanged upstream" does not mean "nothing to fetch" — if WE start requesting a field we did not before (every other spec here does exactly that), a record unchanged upstream still has data we have never seen.
🔴 So the delta must be invalidated when the selection set changes, not only when the record does. Practically: a version stamped alongside the timestamp, bumped whenever fields are added. ⚠️ Without it, adopting any other spec in this set would appear to do nothing for existing records — and would look exactly like the feature being broken.
## Test strategy
- **D1** — A record unchanged since last check is skipped.
- **D2** — A record changed since last check is fetched.
- **D3** — 🚨 A record with no recorded check time is always fetched, never skipped.
- **D4** — 🚨 Widening the selection set invalidates the delta for every record.
- **D5** — A full refresh ignores the delta entirely.
- **D6** — A clock disagreement between us and the source cannot cause a permanent skip.
## ❓ Open — Human Operator
1. Is there a reliable per-video last-checked timestamp today? If not, that half ships first.
  1. ✅ **Decision - **Not if you’re not storing it in the app’s metadata
2. Given it is an optimisation, should it wait until a rate limit is actually hit — or is the point to avoid finding out the hard way? Recommend waiting: the report says the limit is untested, and building against an unmeasured constraint is how the studio-overlap work went wrong the first time.
  1. ✅ **Decision - **wait for issues - don’t build in anticipation of a problem we don’t have.
